findings.message: One shoulder sits consistently lower than the other - level the shoulder line.
Your stride length is away from ideal for your height.
Your left and right sides move by noticeably different amounts.
Your chin drops as you walk; lift the gaze to the end of the runway.
Your arm swing is off - aim for a relaxed, even swing from the shoulder.
Your knee lift does not match a full, controlled stride.
Open the chest and draw the shoulder blades back - presence starts with carriage.
Your head sits off the centre line of your body.
Your two arms swing by different amounts.
Your two legs are not swinging equally.
Your feet are not clearing the floor cleanly.
Add a little controlled torso rotation - the walk currently reads as stiff.

coaching.headline: Beginner walk - 51/100. Start with posture and balance.
coaching.summary: Across twelve criteria your strongest work is posture & spinal alignment, and the biggest single gain available is in shoulder alignment. Work the 3 focus area(s) below before adding anything else.

focus_areas.label: Shoulder Alignment
focus_areas.issue: One shoulder sits consistently lower than the other - level the shoulder line.

focus_areas.label: Stride Length
focus_areas.issue: Your stride length is away from ideal for your height.

focus_areas.label: Body Symmetry
focus_areas.issue: Your left and right sides move by noticeably different amounts.

drills.name: Shoulder reset
drills.instruction: Roll both shoulders up, back and down before each pass; walk keeping the collarbones wide.

drills.name: Mirror check
drills.instruction: Walk toward a mirror and watch the shoulder line stay level across every step.

drills.name: Marked stride
drills.instruction: Tape floor markers at your target stride and walk landing on each one until the length feels natural.

drills.name: Slow-motion stride
drills.instruction: Walk at half speed with a full stride to feel the reach without rushing.

drills.name: Video both sides
drills.instruction: Film from the front and check the left and right swing match in size and timing.

drills.name: Unilateral strength
drills.instruction: Work the weaker side alone - single-leg squats and step-ups - to even out the two limbs.
